Write lists of outputs with flexible organization and naming

Source: R/lwrite.R
lwrite.Rd

Writes nested lists containing plots, tables, and data frames to files with intelligent handling of list structure, automatic naming, and optional subdirectory organization. This is particularly useful for organizing multiple related outputs from a single analysis or model run.

Usage

lwrite(
  list,
  model,
  dir = ".",
  path.format,
  lists.as.subdirs = FALSE,
  name.all.pdf = "main_all.pdf",
  structure,
  ...
)

Arguments

list

A list (potentially nested) containing output objects: ggplot plots, flextable tables, and/or data.frames. The list can be arbitrarily nested, and names at each level will be used to construct output file names.

model

Character string or model object specifying the model name/identifier. Used for organizing output directories and stamping. If a list (model object) is provided, the $label element is extracted.

dir

Character string specifying the base output directory. Default is "." (current directory).

path.format

Character string or function defining the output path format. Passed to pathFormat to create a path-generating function. Examples: "%model/%name_%model" (default), "%name_%model", "%script/%name_%model". See pathFormat for details.

lists.as.subdirs

Logical. If TRUE, nested lists create subdirectories rather than being incorporated into file names. Default is FALSE.

  • FALSE: nested list names become part of file names (e.g., list1_item1.png)

  • TRUE: nested lists create subdirectories (e.g., list1/item1.png)

name.all.pdf

Character string specifying the filename to use when writing all plots to a single PDF file. Only used when the file name is empty and plots are being combined into one PDF. Default is "main_all.pdf".

structure

Deprecated. Use path.format.

...

Additional arguments passed to writer and subsequently to the specific writer functions (ggwrite, ftwrite, or datwrite). Common arguments include:

  • script: Path to script file for stamping

  • time: Timestamp for stamping

  • formats.gg: File formats for plots (default "png")

  • formats.ft: File formats for tables (default "png")

  • formats.data: File formats for data frames (default "rds")

  • canvas: Canvas size for plots

  • quiet: Suppress messages

  • stamp.format, stamp.funs: Stamp text format, see createStamp

  • stamp.gg.style, stamp.ft.style: Stamp styling for plots and tables, see writer

Value

Invisibly returns a list of results from the writer calls. The structure mirrors the input list structure.

Details

The function processes lists recursively with the following behavior:

  1. Separates plot objects from non-plot objects

  2. Combines plots into a single multi-page or multi-file output (see ggwrite)

  3. Writes each non-plot object individually

  4. Handles nested lists according to lists.as.subdirs

List Structure Handling

The function intelligently flattens nested lists while preserving meaningful names:

  • Named list elements use their names in output file names

  • Plots in the same list are combined (behavior depends on ggwrite settings)

  • Non-plot objects (tables, data frames) are written individually

  • Nesting deeper than 2 levels will cause an error

File Naming

Output file names are constructed from:

  • The name at each level of the list hierarchy

  • The model identifier (if provided and if path.format uses it)

  • Automatic numbering for unnamed elements

For example, with lists.as.subdirs = FALSE:


list(
  section1 = list(
    plot1 = p1,
    table1 = ft1
  )
)

produces: section1_plot1.png, section1_table1.png

With lists.as.subdirs = TRUE, the same structure produces: section1/plot1.png, section1/table1.png

Plot Handling

All ggplot objects within the same list level are collected and written together using ggwrite. This allows creating multi-page PDFs or sequentially numbered PNG files from a list of plots.

See also

writer for the underlying writing function, ggwrite for plot-specific options, ftwrite for table-specific options, datwrite for data frame writing, pathFormat for path format options, is.listnotplot for list detection logic

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
library(flextable)

# Create some outputs
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) + geom_point()
ft1 <- flextable(head(mtcars))
df1 <- mtcars

# Simple list
outputs <- list(
  scatter_wt = p1,
  scatter_hp = p2,
  summary_table = ft1,
  data = df1
)

lwrite(outputs, model = "run001", dir = "outputs",script="myscript")
# Creates in outputs/run001/:
#   scatter_wt_run001.png
#   scatter_hp_run001.png
#   summary_table_run001.png
#   data_run001.rds

# Nested list with subdirectories
nested_outputs <- list(
  diagnostics = list(
    gof1 = p1,
    gof2 = p2
  ),
  tables = list(
    summary = ft1
  )
)

lwrite(nested_outputs,
       model = "run001",
       dir = "outputs",
       lists.as.subdirs = TRUE)
# Creates:
#   outputs/run001/diagnostics/gof1_run001.png
#   outputs/run001/diagnostics/gof2_run001.png
#   outputs/run001/tables/summary_run001.png

# With stamping
lwrite(outputs,
       model = "run001",
       dir = "outputs",
       script = "analysis.R",
       time = Sys.time())
} # }
